newsitem.title: CHINA: GM's Delphi unit sees China sales doubling.
newsitem.headline: GM's Delphi unit sees China sales doubling.

text.p: Delphi Automotive Systems, a unit of General Motors Corp, expects its sales in China to double in 1997, an official of the U.S. car component maker's China operations said on Wednesday.
"We hope sales will double to $150 million this year," Marcus Chao, chief representative of Delphi's China operations, told Reuters.
He declined to give a figure for profits or say by how much Delphi planned to invest in China over the next few years.
Chao attributed the expected sales rise to Delphi's joint ventures becoming operational.
"We...are very excited about the future of China's automotive industry," he said.

"There will be many hurdles that the industry will have to get over. But we believe that they will be crossed and that the goal of a viable domestic automotive industry will become reality," Chao said without elaborating.
Delphi's total investment in China to date is about $300 million, with 10 joint ventures and four licence agreements. It has one wholly owned manufacturing base in the southern city of Guangzhou.
The joint ventures employ a total of 4,500 people, while Delphi China itself has about 250 employees.
Delphi's customers in China include most of the country's major automotive manufacturers.
The car component maker stepped up localisation in China in recent years to reduce manufacturing costs.
Delphi, with headquarters in Pontiac, Michigan, is the world's largest supplier of automotive components and systems. It had annual sales of $27.8 billion in 1996.
